errors.description: The abstract misstates HFD exposure as 20 weeks. The animal protocol specifies 12 weeks of treatment starting at 8 weeks of age, making 20 weeks the endpoint age rather than the feeding duration.
errors.evidence: Abstract: "Mice were fed by a 60% kcal fat diet for 20 weeks". Methods: mice were purchased at "5 weeks", randomized "After 3 weeks", and euthanized "After a 12-week treatment".

errors.location: Abstract, Results; animal experimental methods and mouse results
errors.description: The abstract attributes the mouse treatment results to GW4064, but the described mouse experiment used INT-747. GW4064 treatment of mice is not part of the reported protocol.
errors.evidence: Abstract: "Treatment with the FXR agonist CDCA or GW4064 decreased body weight, renal lipid accumulation, as well as renal injury." The four mouse groups were control, HFD, HFD with 0.1% CDCA, and "a 30 mg/kg INT-747 group"; the mouse results likewise report "Treatment with CDCA or INT-747".

errors.location: Mouse characteristics results; supplied textual label for Figure 5H
errors.description: Serum creatinine is reported with incompatible units. The results use micromoles per litre, whereas the supplied Figure 5H label uses millimoles per litre, a factor-of-1000 difference in the concentration scale.
errors.evidence: Results: "serum creatinine (4.8 ± 1.3 vs. 1.11 μmol/L)". Supplied textual label: "Graph H: Serum Creatinine (mmol/L)".

errors.location: Abstract, Results; FXR interaction and AF1 deletion experiments; Figure 4 caption
errors.description: The claimed AF1-mediated binding and disruption of the β-catenin/TCF4 complex are not established by the described assays. The AF1 deletion experiment tests reporter suppression, while the reported co-immunoprecipitation measures FXR–β-catenin association; neither demonstrates AF1-dependent association or loss of TCF4 from that complex.
errors.evidence: Abstract: "We showed that FXR could bind with β-catenin via the AF1 domain, and disrupt the assembly of the core β-catenin/TCF4 complex." The mutant result is that pDEL-FXR "did not have any effect on β-catenin mediated TOPflash reporter activity". The co-immunoprecipitation methods and Figure 4B–C caption specify detection of FXR and β-catenin, without a TCF4 complex measurement.

errors.location: Cell-culture results after Figure 2; opening discussion paragraph
errors.description: Changes in epithelial and myofibroblast markers in an NRK-52E monolayer are treated as confirmation of tubulo-interstitial fibrosis. These measurements show a fibrogenic cellular response, but do not establish fibrosis of a tubulo-interstitial tissue compartment.
errors.evidence: The reported in vitro endpoints are fibronectin, α-SMA, Snail and E-cadherin expression. The discussion calls these changes "confirming that ox-LDL is able to trigger tubulo-interstitial fibrosis" and states that FXR "ameliorates the fibrosis in tubular epithelial cells in vitro".
